title: Diatomaceous Earth–Associated Differences in Soil Fungal Diversity during Maize Cultivation: An Exploratory ITS Metabarcoding Study
content: Soil fungal communities are relevant to the biological condition of agricultural soils, but field observations under siliceous amendments remain limited in tropical maize. We compared fungal ITS profiles from seven composite soil samples: one pretreatment baseline and one sample per management regime at 60 and 120 days after sowing. The regimes were an untreated control, conventional management, and conventional management supplemented with diatomaceous earth. Amplicons were sequenced using Illumina technology and processed with QIIME 2 and DADA2, with UNITE-based taxonomic classification. At 120 days, the conventional sample had lower Shannon (2.806) and Simpson (0.603) indices than the diatomite-supplemented sample (5.896 and 0.956, respectively). Onygenales accounted for 64.89% of reads in the conventional sample; this order was not detected in the corresponding amended sample. Final non-chimeric reads ranged from 13,831 to 74,005, indicating considerable variation in sequence retention. The design provided one molecular profile per treatment–time combination, without independent replication; observed contrasts are therefore descriptive and cannot establish treatment effects. These findings identify testable patterns for replicated field trials integrating fungal sequencing with soil physical and chemical measurements.
